chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'ed Abady quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father and others, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Suleiman al-Sin'ani, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn al-Fazl, on the authority of Aban ibn Taqlib, who said: 'I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)'

When a man from Yemen entered and greeted him, he greeted him back and said, 'Welcome, O Sa'd.' The man said, 'This is the name my mother named me with, and few people know me by it.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'You have told the truth, O Sa'd al-Mawla.' The man said, 'May I be your ransom, that is my nickname.' The Imam said, 'There is no good in the nickname, for God, the Blessed and Exalted, says in His Book: "Nor call each other by (offensive) nicknames: Ill-seeming is a name connoting wickedness, (to be used of one) after he has believed." What is your profession, O Sa'd?'

He said, 'May I be your ransom, I am from a family that studies the stars; we say no one in Yemen is more knowledgeable about the stars than us.' The Imam said, 'Shall I ask you?' The Yemeni said, 'Ask whatever you wish about the stars, for I will answer you with knowledge.' The Imam said, 'How many degrees is the light of the Sun compared to the light of the Moon?'

The Yemeni said, 'I do not know.' The Imam said, 'You have told the truth.' Then he asked, 'How many degrees is the light of the Moon compared to the light of Venus?' The Yemeni said, 'I do not know.' The Imam said, 'You have told the truth.' Then he asked, 'How many degrees is the light of Venus compared to the light of Jupiter?'

The Yemeni said, 'I do not know.' The Imam said, 'You have told the truth.' Then he asked, 'How many degrees is the light of Jupiter compared to the light of Mercury?' The Yemeni said, 'I do not know.' The Imam said, 'You have told the truth.' Then he asked, 'What is the name of the star that, when it rises, causes the cows to copulate?'

The Yemeni said, 'I do not know.' The Imam said, 'You have told the truth.' Then he asked, 'What is the name of the star that, when it rises, causes the camels to copulate?' The Yemeni said, 'I do not know.' The Imam said, 'You have told the truth.' Then he asked, 'What is the name of the star that, when it rises, causes the dogs to copulate?'

The Yemeni said, 'I do not know.' The Imam said, 'You have told the truth in saying 'I do not know.' What is Saturn in your view of the stars?' The Yemeni said, 'A star of bad luck.' The Imam said, 'Do not say that, for it is the star of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and the star of the Trustees (peace be upon them), and it is the Piercing Star about which God, the Mighty and Majestic, said in His Book.'

The Yemeni asked, 'What is meant by 'the Piercing'?' He said, 'Its rising is in the seventh heaven, and it pierces with its light until it illuminates the lowest heaven, for this reason God named it the Piercing Star. O man of Yemen, do you have scholars?'

He said, 'Yes, may I be your ransom, there are people in Yemen who are unmatched in knowledge by anyone else.' The Imam said, 'How knowledgeable are their scholars?' The Yemeni said, 'Their scholar can make birds stop in flight, and can trace the footprints of a fast rider from a month's journey away in one hour.' The Imam said, 'Indeed, the scholar of Medina is more knowledgeable than the scholar of Yemen.'

He asked, 'How knowledgeable is the scholar of Medina?' The Imam said, 'The knowledge of the scholar of Medina reaches where they do not merely stop birds or trace footprints, but they know what distance the sun travels in a single moment: twelve constellations, twelve lands, twelve seas, and twelve worlds.'
The Yemeni said, 'May I be your ransom, I did not think anyone knew this or understood its essence.' Then the Yemeni stood up and left.
ai.seo_question: What is the dialogue between Imam al-Sadiq and the Yemeni astrologer about the stars and knowledge?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) engages a Yemeni astrologer to demonstrate the limitations of celestial knowledge compared to the divine insight of the Ahl al-Bayt. He identifies Saturn as the 'Najm al-Thaqib' (Shining Star), linking it to the Imamate and interpreting the Quranic verse as referring to the Imam's spiritual radiance piercing the heavens. This dialogue underscores the Shia belief that the Imams possess superior, cosmic knowledge that extends beyond the empirical sciences of their contemporaries.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 12-69 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa’ed Abady quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father and others, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Suleiman al-Sin’ani, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn al-Fazl, on the authority of Aban ibn Taqlib, “I was with Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) when some of the people from Yemen came to see the Imam (MGB).

They greeted him (MGB) and he (MGB) greeted them back and said, ‘O Sa’d. You are welcome.’That man said, "This is the name which my mother named me. Few people know me by this name.” The Imam (MGB) said, "O’ Sa’d! O’ Mula! You have told the truth.” That man said, “May I be Your ransom! That is my nickname.” The Imam (MGB) said, "That is not a good nickname. In fact, the Blessed the Sublime God has said in His Book ‘Nor call each other by (offensive) nicknames: Ill-seeming is a name connoting wickedness, (to be used of one) after he has believed.’ A bad name is not suitable for a believer. O Sa’d!

What is your job?” He (MGB) replied, “We are a family of astrologers. No one is more knowledgeable in astrology than we are in Yemen.” The Imam (MGB) said, "Can I ask you some questions about astrology from you (MGB).” He replied, “Yes. Ask whatever you wish to ask and I will give you a scientific answer.”

The Imam (MGB) asked, "How much more is the brightness of the Sun than that of the moon?" He said, "I do not know." He (MGB) said, "You have told the truth.” Then the Imam (MGB) asked, "How much more is the brightness of the moon than that of Venus?” He said, "I do not know".
He (MGB) asked, "What is the name of astar which arouses lust in the cows when it rises to shine? He said, "I do not know?" He asked, "How much more is the light of Jupiter than that of Mercury?"

He said, "I do not know.” He (MGB) asked, "What is the name of the star that the camels copulate when it is seen?" He said, "I do not know." He (MGB) asked, "What is the name of the star that the dogs copulate when it is seen?" He said, "I do not know."

He (MGB) asked, "What is your opinion about Saturn?" He said, "It is a star that brings bad luck" He (MGB) said, "Do not say so because that is Ali’s (MGB) star. It is the star of the Trustees. That is the shooting star about which the Blessed the Sublime God has said, ‘And what will explain to thee what the Night-Visitant is?

(It is) the Star of piercing brightness.’ The man from Yemen asked, “What does Night-Visitant mean?” He (MGB) said, "It rises from the seventh heaven and illuminates all the heavens with its light. For this very reason, the Honorable the Exalted God named it Night-Visitant. O the man from Yemen! Do you have any scholars in Yemen?” He said, "Yes.

May I be your ransom! There are some scholars who have no match in knowledge anywhere.” The Imam (MGB) said, "How knowledgeable are they?” He said, "They can tell fortune with birds. They can tell about the location of the steps of a fast rider one month away in an hour.” The Imam (MGB) said, "Indeed the knowledgeable people of Medina are more knowledgeable than those of Yemen.” He asked, “How knowledgeable are the scholars of Medina?” The Imam (MGB) said, “The knowledge of the scholars of Medina is so extensive that the knowledge of the scholars in Yemen and fortune-telling with birds can never reach it.
They can traverse in a single moment the distance of the path of the rays of the Sun that equals twelve stars, twelve deserts, twelve seas and twelve worlds.”
The man from Yemen said, “May I be your ransom! I do not think that anyone knows this or understands its deep meaning.” Then he stood up and left.
